processes.title: AARTO — Organisational Receiving Process Flow
processes.summary: This flow tells an organisation that owns, operates or allows people to drive vehicles what to do, by when, and who hands off to whom, from the moment an AARTO document arrives until the matter closes and lessons feed back into controls. It is built to comply with the law in force today in the proclaimed municipalities, and to be ready for the points demerit system without redesign.

processes.title: Artificial Intelligence — Organisational AI Compliance and Governance Process Flow
processes.summary: This flow tells a South African organisation what to do, by when, and who hands off to whom, from the moment someone proposes to buy, build or switch on an artificial intelligence (AI) capability until that system is retired and the lessons feed back into policy. It covers predictive and classification models, generative AI (text, image, code and voice), AI agents that take actions on a user's behalf, and automated decision-making in HR and customer processes. It is written for two kinds of organisation at once: the deployer, which uses AI built by others (for example Microsoft 365 Copilot, a recruitment screening platform or a credit-scoring service), and the developer or integrator, which designs, configures or builds AI for itself or for clients (for example agents built in Voiceflow or Microsoft Copilot Studio). Where the two roles carry different duties, the flow says so; Phase 3 has a separate build track (3B).

processes.title: COIDA — Organisational Injury and Disease Claim Process Flow
processes.summary: This flow tells an employer what to do, by when, and who hands off to whom, from the moment an employee is injured or an occupational disease is diagnosed until the claim closes and lessons feed back into controls. It covers reporting, temporary disablement pay, rehabilitation and return to work, incapacity, and the new inspection and penalty regime.

processes.title: Consumer Protection Act — Organisational Complaint Receiving and NCC Compliance Process Flow
processes.summary: This flow tells a supplier what to do, by when, and who hands off to whom, from the moment a consumer complaint arrives — through any of the channels the CPA allows a consumer to use — until the matter closes and lessons feed back into controls. It runs alongside a second, non-case-triggered obligation that the 2026 Amendment Regulations put beyond doubt: registering as a direct marketer on the National Consumer Commission’s (“NCC”) opt-out registry, identifying the organisation in every marketing communication, and cleansing the marketing database against the registry every month. The two are related but distinct: a mishandled complaint exposes the organisation to a compliance notice, a Tribunal referral and an administrative fine of up to R1 million or 10% of annual turnover; unregistered or uncleansed direct marketing exposes it to the same fine once the NCC’s registration deadline (end-December 2026) has passed and full enforcement has begun (15 April 2027), independently of any single complaint.

processes.title: OHSA — Organisational Health and Safety Compliance and Incident Process Flow
processes.summary: This flow tells an employer, or a user of plant or machinery, what to do, by when, and who hands off to whom, from the moment something goes wrong at work until the matter closes and the lessons feed back into the risk assessment. It covers the standing duties that must be in place before anything happens, the immediate response, classification and reporting to the Department of Employment and Labour (DEL), recording and investigation, corrective action and committee review, dealing with inspectors and formal inquiries, and governance. A parallel track covers the continuous risk-management cycle that runs whether or not an incident occurs.

processes.title: Off-Boarding — Organisational Employee Exit Process Flow
processes.summary: This flow tells an organisation what to do, by when, and who hands off to whom, from the moment an exit is triggered until the last dispute window has closed and the exit data has fed the EE plan and retention measures. It is the closing bookend of the GBS employment lifecycle suite: the Resourcing flow brings a person in; this flow takes them out. It runs one core spine for every exit, whatever the reason, and splits only where the law splits — at the legal gate in Phase 1, which fixes the true legal reason for the exit and therefore the notice, pay and procedure that follow.

processes.title: Protected Disclosures — Organisational Receiving Process Flow
processes.summary: This flow tells a receiving organisation what to do, by when, and who hands off to whom, from the moment a disclosure arrives until the case closes and lessons feed back into controls. It is built to comply with the law in force today and to be ready for the Bill without redesign.

processes.title: POPIA — Organisational Compliance Process Flow
processes.summary: This flow tells a South African private-sector organisation what it must do to comply with the Protection of Personal Information Act, by when, and who hands off to whom. It covers the standing programme (Phase 0), every new or changed processing activity (Phase 1), requests from data subjects (Phase 2), security compromises (Phase 3), dealings with the Information Regulator (Phase 4) and the annual cycle of monitoring and review (Phase 5). An employment track (E) applies the same rules to employee and applicant information, and a parallel track (P) covers events that can arise at any time. It is written for Information Officers (IOs), Deputy Information Officers (DIOs), HR, compliance and legal, IT and information security, marketing and line managers.

processes.title: Performance Management, Career and Succession Planning — Organisational Process Flow
processes.summary: This flow tells an organisation what to do, by when, and who hands off to whom, from the moment the strategic plan is approved until the year's ratings have been calibrated, rewarded and turned into development, talent and succession decisions, and the results feed back into the next cycle. It covers the full domain that the GBS Process Architecture assigns to Performance Management, Career and Succession Planning: job profiles, gap analysis, KPA and KPI design and weighting, the gap to the next position, and the 9-box. It is built from the End-to-End Performance Management Process supplied for this flow (1 October 2026), corrected and supplemented as recorded in section 15.

processes.title: Resourcing — Recruitment, Selection and Assessment Process Flow
processes.summary: This flow tells an organisation what to do, by when, and who hands off to whom, from the moment a line manager raises a vacancy until the appointee has passed probation, the recruitment file is archived and the results feed back into the EE plan. It covers internal and external recruitment, promotions and succession appointments, and four ways of engaging the person chosen: permanent employment, a fixed-term contract, a TES placement, or the employment of a foreign national.
